Here are the components used in a manual rear-wheel-drive gearbox:

• Input shaft (Main drive gear/Clutch shaft)

• Countershaft (Layshaft)

• Output shaft (Main shaft)

• Gear sets
  - Constant mesh gears
  - Sliding mesh gears
  - Synchronizer gears

• Synchronizer mechanisms
  - Synchronizer rings
  - Synchronizer hubs
  - Synchronizer sleeves
  - Blocking rings

• Bearings
  - Ball bearings
  - Roller bearings
  - Needle bearings
  - Thrust bearings

• Shift mechanism
  - Shift forks
  - Shift rails
  - Shift levers
  - Detent mechanisms

• Gearbox housing/casing
  - Main casing
  - Front cover
  - Rear cover
  - Extension housing

• Oil seals and gaskets

• Speedometer drive gear

• Reverse idler gear

• Shaft locking nuts and washers

• Selector mechanism
  - Interlock system
  - Gate mechanism

- Gear shafts (input, output, and intermediate shafts)
- Synchronizers for smooth gear shifts
- Gears (including spur gears and helical gears)
- Clutch assembly (Note: The clutch is actually part of the drivetrain between the engine and the gearbox, not inside the gearbox itself)
- Differential unit (responsible for allowing the wheels to rotate at different speeds)
- Bearings to support rotating components
- Housing to protect internal components
- Lubrication system to ensure proper operation and reduce wear

- Input Shaft
- Helical Bevel Gear
- Heavy Flow Clutch Cylinder
- Differential Ring Gear
- Ball Bearing Torque Converter
- Quadratic Output Shaft
- Planetary Gear Cluster
- Synchronizer Hub
- Idler Pulley

- Input Shaft
- Countershaft (also known as the lay shaft)
- Clutch Pedal
- Synchromesh Rings
- Helical Gears
- Drive Shaft (not present in the gearbox itself but integral to rear wheel drives)
- Planetary Gears (common in manual gearboxes)
- Selector Forks
- Shift Linkage
- Differential (always housed within the gearbox)
- Manual Torque Converter
